title: Sequacious
summary: SEQUA'CIOUS, adjective [Latin sequax, from sequor, to follow. See Seek.] 1. Following; attendant. Trees uprooted left their place, Sequacious of the lyre. Dryden. The fond sequacious herd. Thomson. 2.

inlines.v: SEQUA'CIOUS, adjective [Latin sequax, from sequor, to follow. See Seek.] 1. Following; attendant. Trees uprooted left their place, Sequacious of the lyre. Dryden. The fond sequacious herd. Thomson. 2. Ductile; pliant. The forge was easy, and the matter ductile and sequacious. [Little used.] Ray.
